headline: High: B can write and execute against shared files while A is a docs-only content source with broad egress, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing/docs-only agent with broad network egress, while B reads and writes filesystem artifacts and runs shell commands. If A’s output is copied into B’s prompt or files, B can treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks a documented isolation or provenance layer, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is pasted into B’s stdin, prompt, or a file B parses as instructions
IF B processes A-authored content without provenance tagging or sanitization
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Prefix A output with a non-executable delimiter and provenance label
Disable automatic ingestion of A output into B prompts
Review any file passed from A to B before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, and can write/read filesystem artifacts. A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent, so if B’s outputs or files are forwarded to A, sensitive material can leave the local boundary. No profile field shows isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF B reads secrets from files or environment variables and A receives those outputs
IF A forwards B-produced text to a remote endpoint without redaction
mitigations: Do not pass secrets from B into A
Mask environment variables and key material before any handoff
Use separate service accounts and workspaces
Audit A outputs for secret-like strings before transmission
requires-engineering: add automatic secret redaction at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has filesystem write and shell execution; A is a content-writing agent with broad egress. Even though A shows no filesystem write, both can act on shared artifacts if the operator bridges them, creating overwrite or race risk on the same files. Uncertainty remains because A’s IO surfaces are empty, so I choose the higher plausible severity only where shared artifacts exist.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or artifact set
IF A’s generated files are edited or consumed while B is writing them
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for A
Avoid concurrent runs on the same target tree
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestrator coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can execute shell commands and manipulate container artifacts, so if it treats A’s generated content as authoritative, A’s mistakes can become operational actions. A is a docs-only content source, not a verified planner, and no verification step is documented between them. That makes a default-path cascade plausible, though not proven.
conditions: IF B consumes A output as instructions or facts without verification
IF B executes commands derived from A-generated text
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Add a verification step between A and B
Restrict B to dry-run mode for A-derived tasks
Log and diff A output before execution
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, and environment variables, while A has broad network egress. If regulated or secret-bearing data flows from B into A, the pair can create retention or residency issues. A is open-source/docs-only and not a compliance boundary by itself, so the risk is from the handoff path rather than A alone.
conditions: IF B processes regulated secrets or keys and A receives them for summarization or transmission
IF the operator routes EU or PHI-like data through A’s network egress
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A prompts
Classify and block secret-bearing fields before handoff
Use a local-only redaction step
Document retention limits for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
